title: Corporate culture
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:33Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers corporate culture; the closest, the behavioural approach and the internal environment, are related ideas rather than the shared values and behaviours of a business.

draft.title: Corporate culture
card: Corporate culture is the shared values, beliefs and behaviours in a business. It is how people there think and act, and what they accept as normal.
Culture shows up in everyday things: how staff treat each other and customers, how decisions are made, and how mistakes and success are handled.
A positive culture is one where staff feel respected, trusted and part of a team. This tends to lift morale, which is how motivated and satisfied staff feel.
When morale is higher, staff are more likely to stay. This can lower staff turnover and reduce the cost of finding and training replacements.
draft.remember: Culture is how people in a business think and act together. A positive one can lift morale and keep staff.

a.q: Which of these best describes a business's corporate culture?
opts: The shared values and behaviours of its people
The written rules set out in its award
The products it sells and the prices it charges
The number of staff it employs at one time
a.why: Culture is about the values and behaviours people share and accept as normal. A written award sets pay and conditions, which is a different matter from how people think and act together.
a.clue: Think about how people in the business think and act.

b.q: Priya manages a call centre in Newcastle. She starts praising good teamwork, asks staff for ideas and treats mistakes as chances to learn. Over a year, staff feel more valued. What is the most likely effect?
opts: Higher morale and lower staff turnover
Higher morale and higher staff turnover
Lower morale and lower staff turnover
Lower morale and higher staff turnover
b.why: Feeling valued and trusted tends to lift morale, and staff with higher morale are more likely to stay, so turnover is likely to fall. Higher turnover does not fit, because staff who feel respected have less reason to leave.
b.clue: Staff who feel valued have less reason to leave.

a.best: The shared values and behaviours of its people

b.best: Higher morale and lower staff turnover
